overview: This Senate resolution marks the 65th anniversary of NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, founded in 1960. It recalls the center's role in building the Saturn V rocket that carried astronauts to the Moon and its work on Skylab, the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station. It praises the center's leadership of the Space Launch System, NASA's large rocket for the Artemis program to return astronauts to the Moon, and reaffirms the Senate's support for that work. It also honors the center's engineers, scientists and staff. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on July 29, 2025.
for: Supporters say the Marshall center has been central to America's achievements in space for decades and its workforce deserves recognition as NASA aims to return to the Moon.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law, though its endorsement of the Space Launch System touches on an ongoing debate over whether that costly rocket is the best path for NASA.
